index.description: A free, open-source editor that opens DOCX, HWPX, PPTX, PDF, PSD and DWG on one canvas. Keep your work in a single open .omw file and export back to the original format when you share it.

omw.h2:
A working file
that isn't locked up.
omw.lead: A file everyone can use has to be one everyone can open. So .omw has been open from day one.
omw.f1: Open it with any archive tool and look inside, unless it's password-protected.
omw.f2: What goes where inside the package is written down and public.
omw.f3: The code that reads and writes .omw is there for anyone to study and reuse.
omw.goal: Today Omniweave is the only app that opens .omw. The goal is a common format that other tools read and write too.
omw.treeNote: Omniweave reads only scene_graph.cbor and the content pieces; the copies are there for other tools. Every piece is re-hashed on open, and only damaged pieces are skipped.

same.k: Bytes changed on an unedited save

local.d: AI features run on your PC too

proof.notesSummary: How we measured, and the limits
notes: Installer: Omniweave_0.2.0_x64-setup.exe, 17,464,150 bytes (unsigned build). Sizes vary between releases.
Real-world samples: pre-release check on 2026-11-22. Every file ended as full, partial or explained (the app says why it can't open it). File names and contents stay private.
Byte-identical saves: confirmed on every DOCX, HWPX, XLSX, PPTX and PDF sample in the repository, and 259/259 for PSD.
The internet is used only to check for new versions (GitHub Releases).
Encrypted files (PDF AES-256, Office Agile, .omw AES-256-GCM) are encrypted again when you save.
This is an early release. Keep copies of important originals.

loom.lead: Every tile and object gets a content address, so identical pieces are stored once.
loom.moreSummary: How it works and how we measured
loom.thread: 64-bit content addresses for 256px tiles, objects and assets. A repeated tile is stored in the file only once.
loom.weave: A screen tile's key is the hash of the pieces that touch it. There's no invalidation code, so stale pixels can't linger by design.
loom.shuttle: Only new pieces are written to IndexedDB. Autosave stays light and you can recover after a crash.
loom.history: Undo swaps a document reference instead of copying pixels.
loom.canvasAria: Illustration: rub the tile grid and only the tiles you touch are redrawn.
loom.statInit: Rub the grid. Only the tiles you touch are redrawn.

metrics.note: Measured with npm run bench (Vitest bench, Node) on a synthetic 4K document: 42 unique tiles out of 205 references, 51.3 MiB of raw pixels saved as a 1.43 MiB .omw, and undo plus redo in 0.09–0.18 ms (a deep copy of the same document takes 24–28 ms). Save and reopen: 0 damaged, 0 missing. Machine: Intel Core Ultra 5 125H, Windows 11, Node v24.13.1. Drawing time is not included.

items.q: Do I still need my other apps?
items.a: Yes, for now. The aim is to handle many formats in one place; specialist features such as color separations or advanced filters are out of scope today.

items.q: Will I lose anything when I save to another format?
items.a: If something can't be carried over, Omniweave tells you what before it saves.

items.q: How does someone without Omniweave open my .omw?
items.a: Export to the original format, such as DOCX or PDF, and send that. Because .omw is a zip, the images and text copies inside can also be pulled out with other tools.

Each format is labeled full, partial or explained. Some PSD effects and some PPTX shapes are drawn as close approximations, and files that can't be opened, such as HEIC photos, come with a reason. Please report files that don't open well.

oss.lead: The most useful thing you can send is a file that doesn't open properly.
oss.w1: A sample with sensitive content removed is enough.
oss.w2: TypeScript, React, Tauri 2. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the rules.

name.p1: “Ome!” (oh-meh) is what people in Korea's Jeolla region blurt out when something surprises them. It's also the first letters of Omniweave.
name.quote: “All of it in one file? Ome!”

ss.browser: When downloading: if your browser says the file “isn't commonly downloaded”, open the … menu next to it in the downloads list and choose Keep (in Chrome, Keep anyway). New apps get this warning until more people have downloaded them.
ss.unsigned: When running: this build isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may stop it. If you got it from this page and the checksum matches:
ss.signed: The installer is code-signed. If SmartScreen still warns you:
steps: Check that the app name is Omniweave.
ss.warn: If you got the file anywhere else, don't run it.

up.manual: Automatic updates are on the way. Until then:
steps: Download the new installer from this page.
Run it to install over the old version. Your .omw files stay as they are.
up.portable: For the portable app, just replace the exe.
up.auto: Both the installer and the portable app check for new versions on their own. The download is verified first, then you're asked before anything is updated. The Store version is updated by the Store.
up.autoPortable: The portable app checks the size, SHA-256 and signature of the new exe, then replaces itself in place. If it can't write to its folder, it opens this page instead.

ck.p2: with the SHA-256 of every file. If the value you compute matches exactly, the file wasn't altered on the way.
ck.winNote: Compare Hash with the line for the same file in SHA256SUMS.txt (case doesn't matter)
ck.unix: On macOS and Linux, put SHA256SUMS.txt next to the downloaded files and run the command; matching files show OK.

req.wv: Built into Windows 11. On Windows 10 the installer downloads it if it's missing (internet required). The portable app runs only where WebView2 is already installed.
req.perm: Installs for the current user, so no admin rights are needed.
req.web: A recent Chromium-based browser, Firefox or Safari
req.other: Experimental builds. We'll list what's supported once we've tested on real hardware.
req.note: This is an early release. Keep copies of important originals.
